epic.title: Repairs, odd jobs and the house next door
epic.description:
The repairs and odd jobs Phil wants as tickets: the missing fence panel, the boiler flue extension to keep steam off the security camera (a Gas Safe engineer, flue diameter noted first), render patching and paint, the derelict property next door reported (photographs first, then Doncaster Council's current route), the rattling air-conditioning unit, fly screens before summer, and the cast iron weights. The metal gate restoration is not wanted.

## Order
No order is forced. repairs.01 comes before garden.11 (fence treatment, 1 May 2027). repairs.06 has a soft target of May 2027. The rest fit any sitting, with repairs.03 in mild dry weather.

## Done means
All seven closed: the panel in, the flue job booked or done, render patched and painted, the report sent, the rattle gone, screens up, weights indoors.

## Flags
None touch this epic.

## Dossier
The dossier is attached in Docs (link filled by the integrator).

tickets.title: Missing fence panel (about £20 to £30)
tickets.description:
## What
Measure the gap and check the posts are firm, match the style of the neighbouring panels, price and buy a matching panel with clips, and fit it with a helper. Phil's figure was about £20 to £30; two UK suppliers listed a 6 ft by 6 ft overlap panel at about £31 to £35 in 2026 (dossiers/repairs.md, section 3.1).

## Why
Phil wanted the missing fence panel as a ticket.

## Done looks like
The panel fitted, level and firm.

## Unlocks
garden.11: the fence is treated after the panel.

## Depends on
Nothing.

## Cost
About £20 to £35 for the panel plus clips. Nothing is bought in this run.

## Red team
- Finding 68: The panel is a boundary repair outside the garden design rule (H4); Phil confirms on the decisions review.

intro.answer: Measure the gap, buy a matching panel, and fit it between the posts.

sources.label: Less.co.uk: fence panel cost (April 2026 figures)
Atkinsons Fencing: 6ft by 6ft overlap panel
Carvers: lap fence panel listing

steps.title: Measure the gap
steps.body_html: Measure between the posts at top and bottom, and the height of the panels either side.

steps.title: Check the posts
steps.body_html: Push each post. If one moves, the post needs fixing first (a new ticket).
steps.expect_html: Both firm, or a loose one noted.

steps.title: Match the style
steps.body_html: Photograph a neighbouring panel: overlap, closeboard or lap.

steps.title: Price and order
steps.body_html: Price a matching panel at two or three retailers. A 6 ft by 6 ft overlap panel was about £30 to £35 at two suppliers in 2026; budget lines run lower. Order with clips.

steps.title: Fit the clips
steps.body_html: Fix two or three clips to each post at the panel's height.

steps.title: Lift in and fix
steps.body_html: Lift the panel in with a helper, check it is level with its neighbours, and screw through the clips.

tickets.title: Boiler flue extension to keep steam off the camera: note the flue diameter first, then a Gas Safe engineer
tickets.description:
## What
Steam from the boiler flue clouds the security camera. First note the flue's outside diameter (many are 60/100 mm concentric), the boiler make and model, and photograph the terminal with the camera. Then book a Gas Safe registered engineer and ask whether the boiler maker's plume management kit for that model can redirect the plume away from the camera. Phil does not fit it himself.

## Why
Phil wanted the boiler flue extension to keep steam off the security camera, by a Gas Safe engineer, noting the flue diameter first.

## Done looks like
The flue size, boiler model and photos on this ticket, and an engineer booked with a quote.

## Unlocks
Nothing.

## Depends on
Nothing.

## Cost
A plume kit plus an engineer's visit; to be priced by the quote. Nothing is bought in this run.

## Red team
- Finding 69: Quote first; Phil approves before booking.

steps_definition.title: Boiler flue extension: the facts first, then a Gas Safe engineer

intro.answer: Note the flue size and the boiler model, then book a Gas Safe registered engineer; never fit it yourself.

sources.label: Registered Gas Engineer (Gas Safe Register magazine): plume management kits and flue position
Gas Safe Register technical bulletin on plume kits (Registered Gas Engineer site)
Screwfix: Baxi plume kit with 1 m extension, 60 mm (Gas Safe fitting note)
Screwfix: Vaillant plume management kit 100 mm
Gas Safe Register home page (engineer search and ID card check)

steps.title: Measure the flue terminal
steps.body_html: Measure the outside diameter of the flue pipe where it leaves the wall, from the ground if you can (do not climb). Many boilers use a 60/100 mm concentric flue.

steps.title: Boiler make and model
steps.body_html: Read the make and model from the boiler's front or data badge.

steps.title: Photograph the problem
steps.body_html: Photograph the terminal and the camera together, and a camera still showing the steam.

steps.title: Find a Gas Safe engineer
steps.body_html: Search the register for a local engineer, and check their ID card when they arrive.

steps.title: Ask the right question
steps.body_html: Give the make, model and flue size. Ask: does the boiler maker offer a plume management kit for this model, can the terminal be redirected away from the camera within the maker's rules, and what is the price?

notes.html: Flue work is gas work: it must be done by a Gas Safe registered engineer, to the boiler maker's instructions. A plume kit cannot be used to get round a flue that is in the wrong place.

steps.title: Book
steps.body_html: Book the visit and add the date to this ticket.

tickets.title: Render patching and paint
tickets.description:
## What
Tap the render to find hollow areas, check whether it is cement or lime (lime must not be patched with cement), knock off the hollow render, bond with SBR, patch with sand and cement in one or two coats, let it cure three to four weeks, then paint with masonry paint. Mild dry weather only.

## Why
Phil wanted render patching and paint as a ticket.

## Done looks like
All hollow areas patched and the walls painted.

## Unlocks
Nothing.

## Depends on
Nothing. home.20 (plastering) is the learn-it-or-hire-it decision if the areas are large.

## Cost
Bonding agent, mortar and masonry paint; to be priced. Nothing is bought in this run.

## Red team
- Finding 68: Garden-side repair outside the design rule (H4); Phil confirms on the decisions review.

intro.answer: Find the hollow render, check what it is made of, patch it, let it cure, then paint.
to_hand: Sand and cement or a repair mortar
time: About 1 hour over four sittings, with three to four weeks of curing before paint

sources.label: Homebuilding: render repair
DIY Doctor: repairing render
Everest Paints: repairing blown render before painting

steps.title: Tap and mark
steps.body_html: Tap the render; hollow sounds mean it has come away. Mark each area with chalk and photograph it.

steps.title: Cement or lime?
steps.body_html: Look at a broken edge: hard grey and brittle is cement render; soft, crumbly and off-white may be lime. Lime render must not be patched with cement. If unsure, stop and ask Claude with a photo.

steps.title: Weather
steps.body_html: Patch only in mild, dry weather with no frost forecast.

steps.title: Remove hollow render
steps.body_html: Knock off the hollow render back to sound edges. Brush the masonry clean of dust.

steps.title: Bond
steps.body_html: Prime with SBR as its label says (PVA is not for outside).

steps.title: Fill
steps.body_html: Fill with a 4 to 1 sand and cement mix or a repair mortar; two coats if deeper than about 20 mm. Finish with a wooden float, feathering the edges.

phases.title: Paint, three to four weeks later

steps.title: Paint
steps.body_html: Once the patch has cured three to four weeks (fresh cement burns through paint), paint the patched walls with masonry paint.

tickets.title: Derelict property next door: photographs first (the shed on the fence, the exposed sockets), then Doncaster Council's current route, then the report
tickets.description:
## What
Photograph from Phil's own side only: the shed against his fence and the exposed sockets. Then check Doncaster Council's current route (as checked on 2026-11-28: the Nuisance Team for empty or insecure properties and rubbish; Building Control's 24-hour service for a dangerous structure, by phone; the public health team for run-down buildings under section 215), and send the report to the right team with the photos.

## Why
Phil had not yet reported it; the ticket is photographs first, then the report, with the first step checking the council's current route.

## Done looks like
A report sent with photos and a reference or sent date on this ticket.

## Unlocks
Nothing.

## Depends on
Nothing.

steps_definition.title: Derelict property next door: photographs, then the council's route, then the report

intro.answer: Photograph from your own side, check which Doncaster Council team handles it, then report.

sources.label: Doncaster Council: empty properties (Nuisance Team)
Doncaster Council: dangerous structures (Building Control, 24-hour service)
Doncaster Council: unsatisfactory condition or appearance of buildings and land (public health team, section 215)

steps.title: The shed on the fence
steps.body_html: Photograph the shed leaning on your fence from your own side, with the fence in shot.

notes.html: Do not go onto the property.

steps.title: The exposed sockets
steps.body_html: Photograph the exposed sockets only if visible from your side. Do not touch anything.
steps.expect_html: A photo, or a note of where they are.

steps.title: Date and describe
steps.body_html: Write the date and one sentence per photo.

steps.title: Check the current route
steps.body_html: Check the council's pages are as below (they change): empty or insecure properties and rubbish go to the Nuisance Team; a dangerous structure goes to Building Control (24-hour phone line, and they say phone rather than email for danger); a run-down building harming the area goes to the public health team (section 215).

steps.title: Danger first
steps.body_html: If the shed could fall or the sockets could be live and reachable, phone Building Control first.

steps.title: Send the report
steps.body_html: Send the report to the right team with the photos, the address of the empty property, and what it affects. Keep a copy.
steps.expect_html: A reference number or a sent email.

tickets.title: Rattling air-conditioning unit: check the right-side panel fixings before wedging
tickets.description:
## What
With the power off at the isolator, check and tighten the right-side panel's screws on the outdoor unit, check the rubber pads and level, and test. Only wedge something if it still rattles; if it rattles with everything tight, it is an engineer's job.

## Why
Phil wanted the rattling air-conditioning unit as an odd job: check the right-side panel fixings before wedging anything.

## Done looks like
The unit runs without the rattle.

## Unlocks
Nothing.

## Depends on
Nothing.

intro.answer: Power off, check and tighten the right-side panel fixings first; wedge only if it still rattles.

sources.label: Fujitsu General: vibrating outdoor unit mounting rubber
LG: why vibration noise can be heard from the outdoor unit

steps.title: Power off

where.label: The unit's isolator or the fuse box

steps.body_html: Switch the unit off at its isolator or breaker.

notes.html: Never open panels with the power on.

steps.title: Right-side panel
steps.body_html: Check every screw on the right-side panel; tighten any loose one and replace any missing one.
steps.expect_html: No screw turns and the panel does not move when pressed.

steps.title: Pads and level
steps.body_html: Check the rubber feet or pads are there and the unit sits level.

steps.title: Test
steps.body_html: Power on and listen. Only if the rattle remains, wedge a rubber pad where the panel touches, and note where.

troubleshooting.symptom: Still rattles with the panel tight
troubleshooting.fix: It may be the fan or the compressor; that is a job for an air-conditioning engineer.

tickets.title: Fly screens before next summer
tickets.description:
## What
List the windows and doors opened in summer, measure each, choose magnetic (no drilling, cheapest) or roller (screwed in, retracting) screens, and order. Soft target: May 2027, so they are up before summer. No due date.

## Why
Phil wanted fly screens before next summer.

## Done looks like
Screens fitted on each listed opening.

## Unlocks
Nothing.

## Depends on
Nothing.

## Cost
About £15 to £45 per door off the shelf; to be priced per window. Nothing is bought in this run.

intro.answer: Measure the windows and doors that open, choose magnetic or roller screens, and order by May.

sources.label: B&Q: magnetic fly screen door listing
Newblinds: roller fly screens
Moskera: made-to-measure fly screens

steps.title: List the openings
steps.body_html: List which windows and doors are opened in summer.

steps.title: Measure each
steps.body_html: Measure the inside width and height of each opening in millimetres.

steps.title: Choose the type
steps.body_html: Magnetic screens fit without drilling and cost least (about £15 to £45 for a door off the shelf); roller screens screw in and cost more but retract. Nursery window: pick one a child cannot pull down.

steps.title: Order
steps.body_html: Order by May 2027.

tickets.title: Cast iron weights: de-rust, oil, store indoors
tickets.description:
## What
The cast iron weights left outside: brush off loose rust with a brass or nylon brush, soak heavy rust in diluted vinegar for a day, dry immediately and fully, oil thinly, and store indoors off the floor.

## Why
Phil wanted the cast iron weights de-rusted, oiled and stored indoors.

## Done looks like
The weights clean, oiled and indoors.

## Unlocks
Nothing.

## Depends on
Nothing.

steps_definition.title: Cast iron weights: de-rust, oil, store indoors

intro.answer: Brush off loose rust, soak if needed, dry fully, oil thinly, and store them indoors.

sources.label: Jenolite: how to clean rusty weights
Two Rep Cave: restoring rusty weight plates (brush hardness)

phases.title: Cast iron weights: de-rust, oil, store indoors

steps.title: Brush
steps.body_html: Brush off loose rust with a brass or nylon brush (steel scratches cast iron).

steps.title: Soak if needed
steps.body_html: For heavy rust soak in half vinegar, half water for 24 hours, then scrub.

steps.title: Dry fully
steps.body_html: Rinse and dry completely straight away; bare iron rusts again within hours if left wet.

steps.title: Oil and store
steps.body_html: Wipe on a thin coat of light oil, then store indoors off the floor.
